summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: discrete mathematics (sets, permutations, binomial coefficients, induction, modular arithmetic, gcd and the extended Euclidean algorithm, primes), an introductory linear algebra course (vectors, matrices, subspaces, dimension, eigenvalues, the standard dot product and orthogonality over the reals), single-variable calculus (limits, logarithms, exponentials, geometric series, Newton's method), and the standard algorithms and theory courses (asymptotic notation, recurrences, divide-and-conquer such as Karatsuba, amortized binary counters, basic Turing machines). They know binary representation, fixed-width binary arithmetic with carries, and complex numbers including roots of unity, but have not studied the FFT literature in depth, abstract algebra beyond modular arithmetic, tensor products, general bilinear forms, numerical error analysis, or the integer-multiplication research line beyond Karatsuba.

known.name: Big-Omega and Big-Theta notation
known.gloss: f = Ω(g) means f is eventually at least a positive constant times g, and f = Θ(g) means both f = O(g) and f = Ω(g).

known.name: Worst-case running time
known.gloss: The maximum number of steps an algorithm takes over all inputs of a given length n, viewed as a function of n.

known.name: Deterministic algorithm
known.gloss: An algorithm or machine whose next step is uniquely determined by its current state and input, with no randomness or nondeterministic choice.

known.name: Logarithms
known.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which b must be raised to give x; lg usually denotes the base-2 logarithm, and the paper writes lg n = max(⌈log₂ n⌉, 1).

known.name: Iterated logarithm
known.gloss: log* n is the number of times the logarithm must be applied to n before the result drops to at most a fixed constant such as 1.

known.name: Floor and ceiling
known.gloss: ⌊x⌋ is the largest integer at most x and ⌈x⌉ the smallest integer at least x.

known.name: Limits and lim inf
known.gloss: The limit of a sequence is the value its terms eventually stay arbitrarily close to, and lim inf is the smallest value that infinitely many terms approach.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: A sum whose consecutive terms have a fixed ratio r; when |r| < 1 its total is bounded by a constant times its largest term.

known.name: Recurrence relations
known.gloss: An equation or inequality bounding the cost T(n) of a recursive algorithm in terms of its cost on smaller inputs, solved to obtain a closed-form asymptotic bound.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all natural numbers by proving it for a base case and showing that each case implies the next.

known.name: Binary representation
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sum of distinct powers of two, recorded as a string of 0s and 1s ordered by significance.

known.name: Positional radix representation
known.gloss: Writing an integer as a sum of digits times powers of a base q, each digit lying in {0, …, q−1}.

known.name: Binary addition with carries
known.gloss: Adding integers digit by digit from least significant to most significant, passing any overflow in a position as a carry into the next.

known.name: Signed binary numbers and fixed-point numbers
known.gloss: Binary encodings of negative integers (for example by a sign or two's complement) and of fractions as integers scaled by a fixed power of two, where truncation discards the bits beyond the stored precision.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying two n-digit integers by adding shifted copies of one for each digit of the other, using order n² digit operations.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: A divide-and-conquer integer multiplication that replaces four half-size products by three, giving running time O(n^{log₂ 3}).

known.name: Integer division with remainder
known.gloss: For integers a ≥ 0 and b > 0 there are unique q = ⌊a/b⌋ and r with a = bq + r and 0 ≤ r < b.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where two numbers are identified when their difference is a multiple of a fixed modulus Q, so values wrap around to {0, …, Q−1}.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and they are coprime when their gcd is 1.

known.name: Extended Euclidean algorithm
known.gloss: An algorithm that computes gcd(a, b) together with integers x, y with ax + by = gcd(a, b), and hence the inverse of a modulo b when they are coprime.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: If moduli s_1, …, s_k are pairwise coprime, then a residue modulo their product corresponds bijectively to its tuple of residues modulo each s_i.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: An integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The number C(h, k) = h!/(k!(h−k)!) of k-element subsets of an h-element set.

known.name: Sets, Cartesian products and indicator vectors
known.gloss: Basic set operations, including the product A × B of ordered pairs and the 0/1 vector marking which elements of a ground set belong to a subset.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A bijection is a map that is both one-to-one and onto, and a permutation is a bijection of a finite set to itself.

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: Ordering tuples by their first coordinate, breaking ties by the second, and so on, as in a dictionary or row-major storage of a matrix.

known.name: Exclusive or
known.gloss: The bit operation that returns 1 exactly when its two input bits differ, equal to addition modulo 2.

known.name: The two-element field
known.gloss: The set {0, 1} with addition and multiplication modulo 2, in which linear algebra can be done just as over the real numbers.

known.name: Rational numbers and integers
known.gloss: The integers ℤ and the fractions ℚ of integers with nonzero denominators, a dyadic rational being one whose denominator is a power of two.

known.name: Vector spaces and subspaces
known.gloss: A set of vectors closed under addition and scalar multiplication over a field, a subspace being such a subset of a larger space and the span of vectors the smallest subspace containing them.

known.name: Linear independence, basis and dimension
known.gloss: A basis is a linearly independent set spanning a space, and the dimension is the number of vectors in any basis.

known.name: Linear combinations and linear maps
known.gloss: A linear combination is a sum of scalar multiples of vectors, and a linear map is a function preserving such combinations.

known.name: Matrices and matrix multiplication
known.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers that multiply by the row-by-column rule and represent linear maps, including the identity matrix I and the all-ones matrix J.

known.name: Invertible matrices
known.gloss: A square matrix A is invertible when some matrix A^{-1} satisfies AA^{-1} = A^{-1}A = I, which happens exactly when its columns are linearly independent.

known.name: Triangular and diagonal matrices
known.gloss: A lower (upper) triangular matrix has all entries above (below) the main diagonal equal to zero, and a diagonal matrix has nonzero entries only on the diagonal.

known.name: Permutation matrices
known.gloss: A 0/1 matrix with exactly one 1 in each row and column, which permutes the coordinates of a vector.

known.name: Matrix transpose
known.gloss: The matrix obtained by interchanging rows and columns, (A^T)_{ij} = A_{ji}.

known.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
known.gloss: A nonzero vector v with Av = λv is an eigenvector of A with eigenvalue λ.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The dot product x·y = Σ x_i y_i of two coordinate vectors, two vectors being orthogonal when it is zero.

known.name: Kernel and image
known.gloss: The kernel of a linear map is the set of vectors it sends to zero and its image is the set of all its outputs, their dimensions summing to the dimension of the domain.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: A complex number ω with ω^q = 1; the primitive q-th roots are e^{2πik/q} with k coprime to q, and their powers are equally spaced around the unit circle.

known.name: Gaussian function
known.gloss: The function x ↦ e^{-a x²}, a bell-shaped curve that decays faster than any power of x.

known.name: Absolute value and triangle inequality
known.gloss: The size |z| of a real or complex number satisfies |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|, so errors bound by summing their sizes, and the unit disk is the set of complex numbers with |z| ≤ 1.

known.name: Rounding to the nearest integer
known.gloss: Replacing a real number by the integer closest to it, which recovers an integer exactly from any approximation within distance less than 1/2.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: An iterative method x ↦ x − f(x)/f'(x) for solving f(x) = 0 that roughly doubles the number of correct digits per step near a simple root.

known.name: Integer square root
known.gloss: The largest integer whose square is at most a given nonnegative integer a.

known.name: Binary counter and amortized increment cost
known.gloss: Incrementing a binary counter L times flips O(L) bits in total, because bit j changes only once every 2^j increments.

known.name: Stack
known.gloss: A last-in, first-out store in which items are removed in the reverse of the order they were added.

known.name: Tape alphabet, tracks and constant-factor simulation
known.gloss: A Turing machine's finite symbol set can be enlarged to hold several tracks per cell, and a fixed number of extra tracks or tapes changes running time only by a constant factor.

known.name: Pointwise operations
known.gloss: Applying an operation separately to each pair of entries at the same index of two arrays, such as multiplying them entry by entry.

known.name: Polynomial multiplication as convolution
known.gloss: The coefficients of a product of two polynomials are c_k = Σ_{i+j=k} a_i b_j, the convolution of their coefficient sequences.

known.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
known.gloss: A polynomial of degree below n is determined by its values at n distinct points, so polynomials can be multiplied by evaluating, multiplying values, and interpolating.
